changelog.label: Historical conceptual publication
changelog.summary: Original CSM publication. Four governance domains and sixteen original components.
added: Four governance domains: Enterprise, Project, Code, UX

changelog.label: Current specification
changelog.summary: Formalizes CSM into a deterministic governance operating model with machine-readable contracts.
added: Two-axis operating architecture (Domains x Execution Functions)
Governance Contract schema for every component
Objective rules vs human judgment points
unchanged: Four governance domains: Enterprise, Project, Code, UX
Sixteen original components and their names

domains.tagline: Establish the decision context before individual projects improvise it.
domains.centralQuestion: Who has authority, who owns the outcome and risk, and what organizational boundaries apply?

domains.tagline: Make scaling an explicit governance decision.
domains.centralQuestion: What evidence should justify continuing, changing, scaling or stopping an AI initiative?

domains.tagline: AI-generated code is still organizationally accountable code.
domains.centralQuestion: How should software engineering governance change when AI contributes to implementation?

domains.tagline: Governance reaches the people relying on the system.
domains.centralQuestion: What do humans need to understand, supervise, challenge and appropriately use AI-supported outcomes?

components.name: Policy Framework
components.description: AI ethics standards and organizational policies that account for system behavior which may differ from conventional software.

components.name: Risk Assessment
components.description: Risk evaluation that accounts for system behavior which may change over time, including model updates, provider changes, or data drift.

components.name: Data Stewardship
components.description: Governance for datasets that influence ongoing AI behavior, including training data, retrieval sources and operational data.

components.name: Strategic Mandate
components.description: Organizational authority and strategic alignment that defines why AI systems are being deployed and what boundaries apply.

components.name: Business Case Definition
components.description: What problem or value is being tested. The business case defines the hypothesis an AI initiative is evaluating.

components.name: Controlled Testing
components.description: What must be learned before scale. Testing designed to answer specific governance and performance questions.

components.name: Scale Decision Framework
components.description: What evidence justifies broader commitment. Defined criteria for deciding whether to proceed, change or stop.

components.name: Playbook Documentation
components.description: What decisions and learning need to survive beyond the pilot team. Documentation that transfers knowledge to operational owners.

components.name: Development Standards
components.description: Engineering standards that account for AI-assisted development, including review requirements and quality expectations.

components.name: Security Protocols
components.description: Security practices that address AI-generated code, including vulnerability scanning and dependency verification.

components.name: Human Oversight
components.description: Human review of AI-assisted contributions proportionate to risk and consequence.

components.name: Traceability Logging
components.description: Records that provide appropriate provenance for AI-assisted changes where risk warrants it.

components.name: Impact Analysis
components.description: Assessment of how AI-supported outcomes affect individuals, groups and workflows.

components.name: Explainability Design
components.description: Design choices that help users understand system behavior, limitations and appropriate reliance.

components.name: Capability Development
components.description: Training and skill development that enables users to effectively supervise and interact with AI systems.

components.name: Adoption Measurement
components.description: Monitoring of how AI systems are actually used, including feedback and complaints.

executionFunctions.name: Purpose, Scope & Accountability
executionFunctions.question: What is the system for, who is accountable, and what boundaries apply?
executionFunctions.description: Establishes the intended purpose, scope, ownership and accountability boundaries for the AI system.

executionFunctions.name: System, Data & Dependency Mapping
executionFunctions.question: What components, data and dependencies comprise the system?
executionFunctions.description: Maps the system architecture, data sources, model providers, tools and integrations.

executionFunctions.name: Risk, Evaluation & Monitoring
executionFunctions.question: What risks exist and how are they evaluated and monitored?
executionFunctions.description: Identifies, evaluates and continuously monitors risks including drift, performance and security.

executionFunctions.name: Controlled Delivery & Change
executionFunctions.question: How are changes controlled and delivered?
executionFunctions.description: Governs the delivery pipeline, change management, testing gates and deployment controls.

executionFunctions.name: Human Oversight, Feedback & Learning
executionFunctions.question: How do humans oversee, provide feedback and learn from the system?
executionFunctions.description: Ensures human oversight mechanisms, feedback channels and organizational learning loops.

executionFunctions.name: Compliance, Evidence & Assurance
executionFunctions.question: What evidence demonstrates governance and what compliance obligations apply?
executionFunctions.description: Collects, organizes and produces evidence for governance assurance and regulatory obligations.

governanceContracts.name: Policy Framework
governanceContracts.purpose: Ensure AI ethics standards and organizational policies account for system behavior that may differ from conventional software.
governanceContracts.coreQuestion: Are there organizational AI policies that apply to this system, and do they account for adaptive or probabilistic behavior?

requiredInputs.label: AI policy documented
requiredInputs.description: Whether organizational AI policies exist and are documented.

requiredInputs.label: Policy addresses adaptive behavior
requiredInputs.description: Whether policies account for AI behavior that may change over time.

requiredInputs.label: Accountable owner
requiredInputs.description: Named individual accountable for the system.

optionalInputs.label: Policy version
optionalInputs.description: Version of the organizational policy applied.

humanJudgmentPoints.question: Is the use ethically acceptable within organizational values?
humanJudgmentPoints.description: Ethical acceptability cannot be computed from facts alone.

humanJudgmentPoints.question: Does a specific legal obligation apply to this use?
humanJudgmentPoints.description: Legal applicability requires interpretation of regulations against system context.

requiredDecisions.question: Does a specific legal obligation apply?

allowedReasons: Policy under development with interim controls

governanceContracts.sourceProvenance: Original CSM publication, August 29, 2025. V2 contract formalized 2026-08-10.

governanceContracts.name: Risk Assessment

governanceContracts.coreQuestion: Has a risk assessment been performed that accounts for adaptive AI behavior and temporal change?

requiredInputs.label: Risk assessment completed
requiredInputs.description: Whether a risk assessment has been performed.

requiredInputs.description: Whether the assessment considers model/behavioral drift.

requiredInputs.label: Risk assessment date

humanJudgmentPoints.question: Is the residual risk acceptable?
humanJudgmentPoints.description: Residual risk acceptance requires human judgment about risk tolerance.

allowedReasons: Risk assessment in progress with interim risk controls

componentDependencies.rule: Scale decision should not become READY if required controlled testing is incomplete.
Scale decision requires an approved business case.
Human oversight requirements depend on applicable development standards.
Security protocols operate within defined development standards.
Traceability logging follows defined standards for what must be traced.
Explainability design depends on impact analysis to determine what must be explained.
Capability development depends on what users need to understand (from explainability design).
Adoption measurement references impact analysis for what constitutes concerning usage.
Business case should align with strategic mandate.
Business case must operate within policy boundaries.
Controlled testing should address identified risks.
Development standards should reflect approved use case constraints.

requirementStates.NOT_ASSESSED: No evaluation has been performed for this requirement.
requirementStates.NOT_APPLICABLE: The requirement has been evaluated and determined not to apply to this system context.
requirementStates.REQUIRED: The requirement applies and has not yet been satisfied. Work has not begun.
requirementStates.IN_PROGRESS: The requirement applies and work is underway but not complete.
requirementStates.SATISFIED: All applicable objective rules pass and required evidence exists.
requirementStates.PARTIAL: Some but not all required evidence or rules are satisfied.
requirementStates.BLOCKED: A blocking condition exists that prevents progress.
requirementStates.EXCEPTION_APPROVED: An approved exception covers this requirement. The exception has a valid expiration.
requirementStates.HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED: A human judgment point has been reached and requires explicit review.
requirementStates.REASSESSMENT_REQUIRED: A reassessment trigger has fired for this requirement.

domainStates.NOT_STARTED: No applicable components have been assessed.
domainStates.IN_PROGRESS: At least one applicable component is assessed but not all are satisfied or validly excepted.
domainStates.READY_FOR_HANDOFF: All applicable required components are satisfied or validly excepted and no human review remains.
domainStates.BLOCKED: At least one applicable blocking component is BLOCKED.
domainStates.REASSESSMENT_REQUIRED: At least one applicable component requires reassessment.

systemStates.ASSESSMENT_INCOMPLETE: One or more applicable components have not been assessed.
systemStates.GOVERNANCE_BLOCKED: One or more applicable components are BLOCKED.
systemStates.HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED: One or more human judgment points require explicit review.
systemStates.READY_FOR_GOVERNANCE_DECISION: All applicable components are satisfied, validly excepted, or not applicable. No blockers or human reviews remain. A human authority may record an approval decision.
systemStates.REASSESSMENT_REQUIRED: One or more reassessment triggers have fired.

levels.BASELINE: Minimum governance for all AI-enabled systems. Universal requirements apply.
levels.ENHANCED: Additional requirements activated by organization-defined factors beyond baseline.
levels.INTENSIVE: Maximum governance depth for systems with significant consequential, safety, or regulatory exposure.

proportionalityFactors.label: Consequential decisions
proportionalityFactors.description: System outputs influence decisions affecting individuals rights, opportunities, or wellbeing.

proportionalityFactors.label: External customer impact
proportionalityFactors.description: System interacts with or produces outputs for external customers.

proportionalityFactors.label: Sensitive data
proportionalityFactors.description: System processes personal, financial, health, or other sensitive data.

proportionalityFactors.label: Autonomous action
proportionalityFactors.description: System can take actions without per-action human approval.

proportionalityFactors.label: Difficult to reverse
proportionalityFactors.description: System actions are difficult or impossible to reverse.

proportionalityFactors.label: Safety impact
proportionalityFactors.description: System failure could cause physical or psychological harm.

proportionalityFactors.label: Significant financial impact
proportionalityFactors.description: System failure could cause material financial loss.

proportionalityFactors.label: Large affected population
proportionalityFactors.description: System affects a large number of individuals.

proportionalityFactors.label: Critical vendor dependency
proportionalityFactors.description: System depends on a third-party provider whose failure would disrupt operations.

proportionalityFactors.label: External regulatory exposure
proportionalityFactors.description: System is subject to specific regulatory requirements (e.g., EU AI Act, NYC LL144).

provenance.originalArticleTitle: Cognitive System Management: A Framework for Enterprise AI Project Governance
provenance.v2Label: CSM 2.0 is a formalization and extension of the original CSM publication. It does not claim the 2025 article contained V2 features.
provenance.determinismPrinciple: CSM 2.0 makes governance deterministic where objective rules permit and makes human judgment explicit, attributable and traceable where interpretation is required.
provenance.determinismContract: For a fixed CSM specification version, organizational policy configuration, explicit assessment date and normalized input record, objective CSM evaluation must produce the same computed requirement set and statuses.
provenance.legalDisclaimer: CSM 2.0 does not produce legal compliance verdicts. It may produce governance requirements, evidence gaps, review requirements, decision records and framework mappings. Legal applicability or legal sufficiency must remain subject to qualified interpretation where needed.

deterministicDecisions: Whether an accountable owner is assigned (ENT-MANDATE)
Whether a required evidence artifact exists (any component)
Whether an exception has expired (any component)
Whether a reassessment trigger has fired (system-wide)
Whether a dependency is satisfied (component dependency graph)
Whether a component is applicable based on system context (applicability rules)
Whether required inputs are present (input validation)
Whether a domain is ready for handoff (domain state derivation)
Whether a blocker exists (blocking condition check)
humanJudgmentDecisions: Whether a use is ethically acceptable (ENT-POLICY)
Whether an explanation is adequate for affected users (UX-EXPLAIN)
Whether a business benefit justifies risk (PRJ-BUSINESS)
Whether a scale decision should proceed (PRJ-SCALE)
Whether training is adequate for the system (UX-CAPABILITY)
Whether an exception should be approved (any component)
Whether a system is approved for a specific purpose (system-level approval)

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Govern (GV): Policies, procedures, processes, and practices
entries.notes: CSM Policy Framework establishes organizational AI policies. NIST Govern and ISO Clauses 5-6 address organizational context and policy establishment.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Map (MP): Context and risk identification
entries.isoClause: Clause 6.1 - Actions to address risks and opportunities
entries.notes: CSM Risk Assessment identifies AI-specific risks. NIST Map and ISO 6.1 address risk identification and treatment.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Map (MP.2.2): Data provenance and quality
entries.notes: CSM Data Stewardship covers data governance. NIST and ISO address data quality and provenance at the system level.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Govern (GV.2): Accountability structures
entries.notes: CSM Strategic Mandate defines accountability. NIST and ISO address accountability structures.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Map (MP.1): Context establishment
entries.notes: CSM Business Case defines the project hypothesis. NIST Map establishes context. ISO 8.1 addresses operational planning.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Measure (MS): Assessing and tracking AI risks
entries.notes: CSM Controlled Testing evaluates risks before scale. NIST Measure tracks and assesses. ISO 8.3 requires impact assessment.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Manage (MG): Responding to AI risks
entries.notes: CSM Scale Decision is a governance gate. NIST Manage responds to risks. ISO 8.4 addresses change management.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Govern (GV.3): Documentation and transparency
entries.notes: CSM Playbook transfers knowledge. NIST and ISO address documentation and transparency.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Manage (MG.2): Enhancing AI system quality
entries.notes: CSM Development Standards govern AI-assisted code. NIST and ISO address development controls.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Measure (MS.2.8): Security and robustness
entries.notes: CSM Security Protocols address AI-generated code vulnerabilities. NIST and ISO address security testing.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Manage (MG.3): Human-AI configuration
entries.notes: CSM Human Oversight ensures proportionate review. NIST and ISO address human-AI configuration and oversight.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Measure (MS.2.10): Tracking and logging
entries.notes: CSM Traceability Logging records AI-assisted changes. NIST and ISO address logging and records.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Map (MP.3): Potential impacts
entries.notes: CSM Impact Analysis assesses effects on individuals. NIST Map addresses potential impacts. ISO 8.3 requires impact assessment.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Manage (MG.3.2): Transparency and explainability
entries.isoClause: Clause 8.5 - Transparency and information for users
entries.notes: CSM Explainability Design addresses user understanding. NIST and ISO address transparency.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Govern (GV.4): Workforce development
entries.notes: CSM Capability Development builds user skills. NIST addresses workforce. ISO addresses competence and training.

entries.nistReference: NIST AI RMF 1.0 - Measure (MS.3): Feedback and monitoring
entries.isoClause: Clause 9.1 - Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
entries.notes: CSM Adoption Measurement monitors usage and feedback. NIST Measure addresses monitoring. ISO 9.1 requires monitoring.

nistIsoCrosswalk.disclaimer: This crosswalk is informative. It does not constitute equivalence, certification, or a compliance guarantee. CSM 2.0 is an independent governance methodology. NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001 are separate frameworks with their own scopes, definitions and requirements. Organizations seeking certification or compliance with NIST or ISO should consult the original standards and qualified assessors.
